items.markdown:
The **Manifesto for Agile Software Development** is `a foundational 2001 document written by 17 software practitioners at Snowbird, Utah, to replace rigid, heavy, documentation-driven development methods with an adaptive, human-centric approach`.[[1]](https://agilemanifesto.org/)[[2]](https://www.pmi.org/disciplined-agile/agile/theagilemanifesto)[[3]](https://www.atlassian.com/agile/manifesto)[[4]](https://business.adobe.com/blog/basics/agile-manifesto)

### The Four Core Values

The manifesto establishes four primary value pairs, emphasizing the items on the left while still recognizing the value of the items on the right:[[1]](https://agilemanifesto.org/)[[2]](https://business.adobe.com/blog/basics/agile-manifesto)

- **Individuals and interactions** over processes and tools
- **Working software** over comprehensive documentation
- **Customer collaboration** over contract negotiation
- **Responding to change** over following a plan[[1]](https://agilemanifesto.org/)


---

### The 12 Principles
The core values are supported by 12 guiding principles for teams:[[1]](https://www.pmi.org/disciplined-agile/agile/theagilemanifesto)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bz7paA0-oVY&vl=en&t=2)

1. **Satisfy the customer** through early and continuous delivery of valuable software.
2. **Welcome changing requirements** , even late in development.
3. **Deliver working software frequently** , ranging from a couple of weeks to a couple of months.
4. **Collaborate daily** between business stakeholders and developers throughout the project.
5. **Build projects around motivated individuals** , giving them the environment, support, and trust they need.
6. **Use face-to-face conversation** as the most efficient and effective method of conveying information.
7. **Working software** is the primary measure of progress.
8. **Maintain a sustainable pace** , allowing sponsors, developers, and users to keep a constant speed indefinitely.
9. **Enhance agility** through continuous attention to technical excellence and good design.
10. **Practice simplicity** , maximizing the amount of work not done.
11. **Foster self-organizing teams** to architect, requirements, and designs best.
12. **Reflect and adjust regularly** , having the team tune its behavior at regular intervals to become more effective.[[1]](https://www.agilealliance.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/agile-manifesto-download-2025.pdf)[[2]](https://www.pmi.org/disciplined-agile/agile/theagilemanifesto)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v0h9yyGDIC8)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bz7paA0-oVY&vl=en&t=2)

You can read the complete text directly on the [Official Agile Manifesto Website](https://agilemanifesto.org/) or explore broader concepts via the [Agile Alliance](https://agilealliance.org/agile101/the-agile-manifesto/).[[1]](https://agilemanifesto.org/)[[2]](https://agilealliance.org/agile101/the-agile-manifesto/)Would you like to explore how these values apply to a specific framework like **Scrum** , or how to introduce Agile principles to a traditional team?
